extra: The first stage load reaches this window. Code, map data and any padding still need their exact boundaries.
Second stage payload loaded at $C800. Individual asset boundaries remain to be classified.

comments.text: Build the shape number from the actor's animation selector. On a rare random result adjust Y by toggling bit one. The selector chooses left or right motion by one pixel, with a screen-boundary test.
Initialize the slot counter to seven when its current shape is zero. Refresh the base shape and use a random test to choose between the ordinary drift and the state-change path.
Move X one unit toward $20 when left of Arthur and toward $90 otherwise. Move Y toward $44 while between $44 and $BF, and increment it outside that interval.
Use a five-bit random value. Results below four set type $3F with a delay of $14, while values four through seven set type $3E. Otherwise prepare the arc if the actor is close enough horizontally.

Compare the horizontal distance to Arthur against $40 and save the distance when closer. Save the starting Y and choose the vertical amplitude from another random test and the vertical distance. Pick the angle step and start angle from the side of Arthur, save Arthur's X as the centre and advance the actor type.
Twenty-four per-slot horizontal centres used during the arc. $87EB stores Arthur's X here when starting the arc.
Twenty-four per-slot vertical centres. Arc setup stores the initial actor Y here. Type $3E reuses the same field for its target Y.
Compute the arc coordinates from the current angle, amplitudes and per-slot centres. Add the angle step and return to the previous actor type when the angle masked with $7F reaches $40.
Enter the resident overlap handler at $397F with Y set to two.
Set the target Y to Arthur's Y minus $15. Move vertically by a pixel toward it, then restore type $3C and try the arc setup once it is reached.
Decrement the countdown. In the range five through fourteen, choose shape $85 and try starting a linked type $40 actor when no such slot is active.
Pick shapes $86 and $87 using bit three of the phase counter at $BC.
Use bits two and three of $BC for shape $88 through $8B, then jump to the resident motion helper.

Compare the parent actor's X with Arthur's X and divide the result into three distance bands. Load the corresponding entry from $88F2 and call the resident linked actor allocator with type $40 and Y set to two.
Three horizontal motion values chosen from the signed distance to Arthur in the type $40 spawn path.
Clear the motion flag, choose an initial vertical step of two or four and set a random delay between $10 and $2F. Advance the type and set shape $75.
Four entries chosen by the low two random bits for the initial vertical step.

Move left and update Y using the low seven bits of the step. The high bit selects upward motion. On phase zero reduce the magnitude when rising and increase it when falling. Terrain properties can flip the direction and set the IRQ operand at $5D07 to $0E.

Retire when $FB is negative. With a clear state, alternate shapes $83/$84. Bit two in the four contact cells at $2945 permits a limited number of activations, choosing a facing from Arthur's X and moving the actor down four pixels.
State one samples terrain six pixels above the slot before moving toward Arthur. Other positive states move along the return step and clear the state after the countdown expires.
Two signed X steps used when approaching Arthur, indexed by facing.
Two signed X steps opposite the approach steps, used in the return phase.

Animate from shape $8F and set a horizontal step toward Arthur once the animation passes $9A. In its moving phase choose one of four shapes, add both coordinate steps and remove the slot if it leaves the bounds.
End the opening animation at shape $8C. Choose X step plus or minus two by comparing the actor with Arthur, then set the initial Y step from two random bits.
Four shapes for the moving phase, indexed by the slot's animation counter.
Set a counter of $10, clear movement state, reset the pose and linked-spawn counters, then select a random delay and advance to type $43 with shape $9B.

From idle, age the delay and use distance to Arthur and random tests to choose a new action. State one makes a short facing-dependent move. State two builds the curved movement and can spawn a linked actor.
Enter state two and patch the arc angle, horizontal origin and radius operands. Set the two signed angle steps and initialize the short delay.
Type $42 clears this operand. The arc setup masks it to two bits to select the radius and step, then increments it for the next selection.
State one animates and moves horizontally toward Arthur until the timer expires. In state two update facing, move until close to Arthur and then compute the arc position.

Advance the angle with the signed step. Reset the movement at the end of the angle range. Otherwise use the resident projection helpers to place the slot and select its pose. With a large radius and qualifying random bits, spawn a type $62 slot.
The angle used by the projection helpers is stored in the immediate operand at $8BFF. The arc setup seeds it and each step adds the signed direction value.
The arc passes this radius to the horizontal projection at $8C0E.
Arthur's X at the start of the arc is added to the horizontal projection here.
The arc passes this radius to the vertical projection. The value also gates the type $62 spawn path.
Use the pose including its facing bit to write the descriptor pointer and its two extents into the resident shape tables, then run the common hit check.
Choose shape $94 or $95 from the phase. Run the hit check with parameter $11, and decrement the linked-spawn count when the slot changes type.
Two shape codes selected by the phase at $8CA4.
Two starting arc angles selected by the facing at $8B65.
Four pose values indexed by the animation phase and combined with facing.
Two opposite signed steps filled by $8CD1 and indexed by facing.
Receive the negation of the first direction step at $8CD9.
Cleared by type $42 initialization, incremented when the arc spawns type $62, and decremented when that slot changes type.
Four projection radii indexed by the masked pose counter.
Four step magnitudes selected alongside the arc radius and passed to the step setter.
Four packed signed values below the setter entry. The indexed read at $8B76 selects only the preceding four entries.
Store the input and its two's complement in the two direction step entries.
Store the absolute X distance to Arthur at $02 and the side at $03. Copy that side into the low bit of the pose and return the distance in A.
Twelve low bytes paired with the high bytes at $8D0A. Each resolved pointer selects a composite shape descriptor.
Twelve page bytes paired with $8CFE, all selecting page $8D.
Twelve horizontal extents paired with the descriptor pointers and copied to $21DF.
Twelve vertical extents copied to $22DF.
Twelve sprite descriptors selected by the pointer tables at $8CFE and $8D0A. Each has a piece count, shared colour and one sprite pointer and coordinate pair for each piece.
Give the slot a counter of two, set a random delay, advance to type $45 and start at shape $9E.
Age the delay before an attack, then count down the animation on even phases. At index three call $88CD to spawn type $40 and clear its delay. Run the common hit check with parameter two.
Six shape numbers read backwards as the attack animation ages.
Ten coarse horizontal coordinates for the first frame hook. It also tests the next coordinate to choose a second path.
Ten values compared with $FD alongside the matching column tests.
Even offsets into the resident map pointer table at $4CF0 to resolve the chunk to edit.
Within-chunk columns added to the row offsets chosen by the next table.
Indexes into the row offset table at $1BD6 for the chunk edits.
Ten selectors for the tile patterns that $8FB7 dispatches.
Four coarse X values. On an exact match the update sets the corresponding inactive edit counter to seven.
Four live counters. The update decrements a positive counter and uses the result to index all six row and side tables.
Four low bytes of the first destination pointer, one per trigger.
Four high bytes paired with $8E94 for the first destination.
Four low bytes of the other destination pointer used in the paired tile writes.
Four high bytes paired with $8E9C.
Two exact coarse X positions that activate the moving column edits.
Two live column pointer low bytes, adjusted after each edit step.
Two live high bytes for the pointers whose low bytes are at $8EA6.
This countdown starts at $FF and ages toward zero after the first trigger column is reached.
The second column uses its own countdown and pointer. Its tile writes substitute offsets for part of the row.
The two initial countdowns copied to $8EAA/$8EAB when their triggers are reached.
Two low bytes followed by two high bytes copied into $8EA6–$8EA9 by $9007.

Run the stage check at $91A7. At column $77 and beyond set the flag at $4728. At $BC and beyond advance the stage section and reinitialize scrolling. Compare four trigger positions from $8E8C with the current column.
On phase two exchange 80 character pattern bytes at $F4C0 and $F510. Then check the two halves of trigger positions against Arthur's map coordinate.
Clear the terrain property at $B92D. Set the four trigger flags and both column counters to $FF and restore the two packed column pointers from $8EAE.
Seven top-row tile codes for the first destination, read at $8F11.
Seven top-row tile codes for the second destination, read at $8F16.
Seven tile codes written 20 bytes after the first destination.
Seven tile codes written 20 bytes after the second destination.
Seven tile codes written 40 bytes after the first destination.
Seven tile codes written 40 bytes after the second destination.

At horizontal position $F8 or at the specific $010F/$0C combination, call $4873 if $E9 has its high bit set. Select the alternate sprite colour set and update terrain properties according to the horizontal position.
Below position $D5 select colour set four and write zero at $B92D. At exactly $D5 clamp Arthur's Y to $8B when it exceeds that value. Above $D5 select set five and set bit seven in the property.
Select one of two value pairs at horizontal position $EA and write the pair into $B90C and $B90D.
At a horizontal position of at least $0110 with the high byte equal to one, call $2F17 when $D6 is zero.
Call the spawn helper at $9264 and the trigger helper at $8ECF. At horizontal position $BC rerun the section setup.

On phase zero, use the two pointers at $8EA6/$8EA8 and their countdowns. Activate a negative countdown at its trigger X, write the corresponding start tiles, or write another active step when the counter is positive.
Subtract 20 to move to the preceding row. Save the updated pointer, write the four tile values at row-relative offsets and decrement the active counter.
The zero high-byte operand of the subtraction at $9122. The remaining code stores the column pointer's high byte and finishes writing the four tiles from right to left.
Pick one of eight pointers using the low three phase bits. Walk backwards across sixty bytes and toggle the low bit of any tile in the inclusive range $C7 through $D8, relative to $C7.
Low bytes of the eight terrain pointers read by $914B.
High bytes paired with the table at $916C.
Replace six resident shape operands with the sequence $60 through $65 and four more with $5C through $5F.
Choose the scrolling-region path from $CB. At the starting region, rate-limit on $BC and the random bit, then test current tile attributes before permitting an extra actor.
Read the selected tile property. A nonzero property identifies a row for spawning the actor at the right edge.

Require no optional actor and a zero four-bit random sample. Allocate a type $3A slot, place it at one of two side positions with a random Y offset from Arthur and initialize its direction, shape and counter.
The initial screen X positions for the side bit selected by $923F.
Below coarse region $0F, check $9D, existing type $43 slots, phase, a random bit and the optional actor count before allocating type $41.
At coarse region $0C or beyond place the new actor at one of sixteen X coordinates and choose Y from $92DD. Set shape $8F.
Below coarse region $0C choose a side from $9262 and a Y coordinate from eight possible offsets. Enter the type $41 setup helper.
Two screen Y positions selected by the low random bit at $92B1.

Section 02 has 6 ordered spawn records. Each six-byte record contains a 16-bit X tile, a 16-bit Y tile, packed sub-tile offsets and the actor ID. The scan at $30B3 advances after allocating the actor.

Section 03 has 3 ordered spawn records. Each six-byte record contains a 16-bit X tile, a 16-bit Y tile, packed sub-tile offsets and the actor ID. The scan at $30B3 advances after allocating the actor.
Section 02 and 03 has 0 optional spawn positions. Each record holds the two tile coordinates and one packed sub-tile byte. The bounded search at $3175 tests visibility and a random condition.
Reset the terrain triggers and send the map edit stream at $936A to the resident map writer.
Reset the terrain triggers, install the stage-two actor shapes and send the map edit stream at $931E to the resident map writer.
Commands for the resident map writer starting at $2FCD. The setup at $9311 selects this stream.
Commands for the resident map writer starting at $2FCD. The setup at $9307 selects this stream.
Three little-endian start addresses for stage 2 music. The resident stage setter copies the six bytes into index six of the SID song table.
Stage 2 supplies this starting address for voice 1 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Stage 2 supplies this starting address for voice 2 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Stage 2 supplies this starting address for voice 3 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Continuation of the stage 2 tune region. Following command targets from its three starting pointers reaches the last phrase bytes at $9A51.
The current packed stage payload includes a byte-for-byte copy of stage 1 music data through $9D01. The three active pointers refer to their own earlier sequence region.
Zero-filled end of the loaded stage music window through $9FFF. Terrain chunk entries start after the $A000 page boundary.
Loaded 32-byte prefix before the first 200-byte terrain chunk. The entry snapshots share byte $55 followed by zeros. Layout pointers start at $A020.

Use the tile code as the index into the $B6 page selected by $2EEF. $48CC subtracts the selected byte from the player's ground-aligned Y value.
Surface offsets for the other terrain bank. $2EEF loads $B7 as the page for the pointer at $C4/$C5.
Tile properties for the first terrain bank. $3C29 maps nearby character-screen positions through this table and stores the attribute bytes at $EE-$F5.
Second terrain bank's tile attributes. $2EEF selects page $B9 for the pointer at $C2/$C3.
Two entries rewritten by the frame hook at $909E and $90A1. The other bytes through $B92C are second-bank terrain properties loaded with the stage.
The second character property of the pair chosen by $9090. The rest of the span holds the following character properties.
The frame hook writes the property for character $2D here. The rest of the page through $B9FF holds the subsequent characters' properties.
Colour lookup by terrain character code. The first bank case in $2EEF selects this page for $4BF8.
Colour lookup by terrain character code. The second bank case in $2EEF patches $4BF8 to this page.
Top-left character codes indexed by the tile number. $5010 and $5027 read this page.
Top-right character codes paired with the left half by $4FF6. $5016 and $5031 read this page.
Bottom-left character codes for the lower half of each tile. $5057 and $506E read this page.
Bottom-right character codes for the lower half of each tile. $505D and $5078 read this page.
Eleven 64-byte VIC sprite slots starting at pointer $20. These slots match in all five stage images and render projectile silhouettes and small circular effects.

Stage sprite slots at pointers $2B through $97. Includes the winged figures, blobs and large segmented enemy pieces visible in the rendered sheet. The 64th byte of each slot is outside the 24 by 21 pixel raster.
Start of sprite 3B in stage 2. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes.
Start of sprite 40 in stage 2. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes. The VIC sees these shapes in RAM beneath the CPU I/O window.
Start of sprite 50 in stage 2. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes. The VIC sees these shapes in RAM beneath the CPU I/O window.

Offset 29 of sprite 83 in the stage 2 art. The VIC sees this RAM as part of a graphics slot.
Start of sprite 90 in stage 2. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes.
Offset 26 of sprite 96 in the stage 2 art. The VIC sees this RAM as part of a graphics slot.
Eight sprite slots starting at pointer $98. These match in all five graphics loads. The rendered slots include small burst and narrow upright shapes.
The second terrain character set. Its 256 eight-byte glyphs are selected by the $0A entry at $5D87 in the terrain bank table.
Stage 2 terrain charset at E800, glyph 80, row 0. The bytes are VIC pixel rows for the terrain cells. Eight bytes form one character.
The first terrain character set. Its 256 eight-byte glyphs are selected by the $0C entry at $5D86 in the terrain bank table.
Stage 2 terrain charset at F000, glyph 7A, row 5. The bytes are VIC pixel rows for the terrain cells. Eight bytes form one character.
Ten complete eight-byte glyphs in the first terrain character set. The helper at $8F41 exchanges these bytes with the ten glyphs at $F510.
Ten more glyphs used in the exchange. The routine visits every byte in both ranges in descending index order.
Continuation of the first terrain character set after the two exchanged glyph ranges. The VIC reads these patterns from bank $C000.
Stage 2 terrain charset at F000, glyph B5, row 7. The bytes are VIC pixel rows for the terrain cells. Eight bytes form one character.
Stage 2 terrain charset at F000, glyph BA, row 2. The bytes are VIC pixel rows for the terrain cells. Eight bytes form one character.
